age.evidence: 5- to 8-week-old homozygous Fezf2-2A-CreER and PlexinD1-2A-CreER mice were used for viral injection, then tested 2 weeks later

dosing.evidence: psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.)... psilocybin (0.1 mg/kg i.p)

group_housing.evidence: Animals were housed in groups with 2 - 5 mice per cage in a temperature-controlled room

day_night_flipped.evidence: operating on a normal 12 hr light - 12 hr dark cycle (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM for light). All behavioral assays were conducted between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM

assays.assay_description: Mouse placed in plexiglass chamber (4x4x4 inches), video recorded for 10 min immediately after psilocybin (1 mg/kg) injection. Head twitches scored manually from video by blinded experimenter. Tested across DREADD-mediated PT/IT silencing and Htr2a knockout conditions.

application_type.evidence: psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline (10 mL/kg, i.p.) was injected

setup_habituation.evidence: no setup habituation mentioned for HTR chamber

setup_restrain.evidence: each mouse was immediately placed into its own plexiglass chamber

food_restriction.evidence: no food in plexiglass chamber during 10 min recording

water_restriction.evidence: no water in plexiglass chamber during 10 min recording

time_to_assay.evidence: After the injection, each mouse was immediately placed into its own plexiglass chamber

sample_size.evidence: n = 11-20 mice in each group (PT/IT studies); n = 6-9 mice in each group (Htr2a)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin reliably induced head twitches. The response was not affected by DREADD-mediated silencing of frontal cortical PT or IT neurons, nor by local Htr2a knockout in medial frontal cortex. However, constitutive CaMKII-driven Htr2a knockout markedly reduced head twitches.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin induced head twitches in our mice as expected, which was not affected by the DREADD-mediated silencing of frontal cortical PT or IT neurons

B7_automated_classification.evidence: videos were scored for head twitches by a different experimenter blinded

E3_bedding.evidence: chambers cleaned with 70% ethanol between mice

E7_social_context.evidence: each mouse was immediately placed into its own plexiglass chamber

assays.assay_description: Active avoidance shuttle box (8''x8''x6.29''). Two induction days of inescapable footshocks (360 shocks, 0.2 mA, 1-3 s) followed by drug administration after second induction, then test session on day 3 with 30 escapable footshocks (0.2 mA, 10 s, 30 s ITI). Escape failures measured.

application_type.evidence: psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline was injected 15 min later

setup_restrain.evidence: Movement of the mouse was captured by beam breaks in the shuttle box

food_restriction.evidence: no food in shuttle box during test

water_restriction.evidence: no water in shuttle box during test

time_to_assay.evidence: 10-15 min after the end of the second induction session... psilocybin... On day 3, one test session was conducted

sample_size.evidence: n = 13-16 mice in each group (Fezf2); n = 11-14 (PlexinD1); n = 8-13 (Htr2a)

outcomes.summary: A single dose of psilocybin reduced escape failures relative to saline. The effect was abolished by chemogenetic silencing of frontal cortical PT neurons during drug administration, but not by silencing IT neurons. Local Htr2a knockout in medial frontal cortex also abolished psilocybin's effect.
outcomes.statistics: interaction effect of treatment × DREADD: P < 0.001, two-factor ANOVA
outcomes.evidence: A single dose of psilocybin reduced escape failures... This psilocybin-induced relief... was abolished if frontal cortical PT neurons were silenced during drug administration

B6_cognitive.evidence: learned helplessness paradigm requires associative learning

E6_spatial.evidence: shuttle box auto door separating the two compartments (8'' x 8'' x 6.29'')

D1_continuity.evidence: induction day 1, induction day 2, test day 3 - data recorded across sessions

D2_session_duration.evidence: 30 trials × ~30 s ITI + up to 10 s shocks ≈ 20 min test session

D3_recording_days.evidence: Day 1 and Day 2 induction sessions plus Day 3 test session

D4_baseline.evidence: induction sessions are stress induction, not baseline behavioral measure of same construct

D5_followup.evidence: test conducted ~24 hours after psilocybin administration

assays.assay_description: Mouse suspended by tape from metal bar 30 cm above floor in sound-attenuating cubicle, plastic anti-climb tube around tail base. 6-min video recording. Immobility time scored manually by blinded experimenter. Tested 24 h after psilocybin (1 mg/kg or 0.1 mg/kg) injection.

application_type.evidence: psilocybin (0.1 mg/kg i.p) or saline (10 mL/kg, i.p.)

setup_restrain.evidence: An animal was suspended from the metal bar by securing its tail to the bar using removable tape

time_to_assay.evidence: Animals were tested 24 hours after administration of psilocybin

sample_size.evidence: n = 10-14 mice in each group (Fezf2); n = 9 each (PlexinD1); n = 8-9 (Htr2a)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (administered 24 h prior) significantly reduced immobility time in the tail suspension test. This effect was abolished specifically by chemogenetic inactivation of frontal cortical PT neurons during drug administration, and by local Htr2a knockout in medial frontal cortex. Silencing IT neurons had no effect.
outcomes.statistics: interaction effect of treatment × DREADD: P < 0.001, two-factor ANOVA
outcomes.evidence: Mice treated with psilocybin 24 hours prior to testing showed a significant reduction in immobility time compared to saline-treated animals

B4_ethological.evidence: TST immobility is not an ethological behavior

B7_automated_classification.evidence: video scoring was done by a different experimenter blinded

D1_continuity.evidence: Videos of the suspended animals were recorded for 6 minutes

assays.assay_description: 14 days of chronic restraint stress (3 h/day), then fear conditioning (day 1, context A, 5 tone-shock pairings, 0.8 mA), psilocybin administered, fear extinction tests (day 3 extinction 1, retention 1, retention 2 on day 17) in context B. Freezing measured via VideoFreeze software.

application_type.evidence: DCZ (0.1 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline... psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: the mouse was brought to the behavior room for habituation for ~30 min

setup_restrain.evidence: mouse was conditioned individually in a chamber and given 3 minutes to habituate (freely moving during recording)

food_restriction.evidence: no food in fear conditioning chamber

water_restriction.evidence: no water in fear conditioning chamber

time_to_assay.evidence: Then 45 min later, we started test for fear extinction, while the drug is presumably still present in the brain

sample_size.evidence: 58 Fezf2-2A-CreER mice injected with DREADD or control viruses, including 17, 13, 13, 15 per group

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin facilitated fear extinction in chronically stressed mice. The effect required frontal cortical PT neurons, as chemogenetic silencing during drug administration abolished psilocybin-driven facilitation of fear extinction.
outcomes.statistics: see Extended Data Fig. 9; two-factor ANOVA with treatment × DREADD interaction
outcomes.evidence: frontal cortical PT neurons are needed for psilocybin-driven facilitation of fear extinction in chronically stressed mice

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: freezing analyzed across multiple CS presentations within sessions

B6_cognitive.evidence: fear conditioning and extinction require learning and memory

E3_bedding.evidence: stainless-steel grid floor; white smooth floor in context B

E6_spatial.evidence: single conditioning chamber with blank walls

D1_continuity.evidence: Day 1 conditioning, Day 3 extinction 1, retention 1, Day 17 retention 2

D2_session_duration.evidence: fear extinction sessions typically include many CS presentations spanning >15 min

D4_baseline.evidence: Day 1 fear conditioning recorded before drug administration on Day 3

judge_notes: Only one candidate (qwen) provided output; reconciled by checking each item against the paper text directly.

Excluded as not behavioural assays: two-photon dendritic structural imaging, two-photon dendritic calcium imaging, in vivo Neuropixels electrophysiology, slice electrophysiology, qPCR, FACS, single-cell transcriptomics, confocal spine morphology — all are imaging/recording/molecular endpoints, not behaviour.

Retained 4 distinct behavioural assays: head-twitch response, learned helplessness, tail suspension test, and stress-induced fear extinction. The fear conditioning/extinction/retention sequence is treated as a single assay per rubric (different phases of same paradigm).
Corrected age_min/max_days to 35-56 (5-8 weeks at viral injection) since testing started shortly after.
Set learned helplessness D2 to '15-60 min' (30 trials × ~30s ITI ≈ 15-20 min) and D3 to '2-7' since induction sessions on days 1-2 record beam-break behavioral data plus test day 3.
Set fear extinction B2 to Yes (freezing analyzed per CS bin within sessions is standard for VideoFreeze output reported in Extended Data Fig. 9).
TST setup_restrain scored 'yes' per rubric (tail-suspended is restrained during recording).
